rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Two transmissions, through Abu Hurayra and through ʿAli, relate that the opening sūra, the Throne Verse, ‘God bears witness,’ and this supplication clung to the Throne and pleaded not to descend; God promised great rewards for reciting them after obligatory prayers.
rows.anchor: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «لما أراد الله أن ينزل فاتحة الكتاب

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Muʿadh had missed Friday prayer while avoiding a Jewish creditor; the Prophet taught him this verse and a prayer to the Merciful for relief, promising repayment even for debt equal to the earth filled with gold.
rows.anchor: قل اللهم مالك الملك.. إلى قوله: بغير حساب، وقل: «يا رحمن الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the Prophet had asked God to place Persian and Roman rule in his community, and this verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: ذكر لنا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سأل ربه أن يجعل ملك فارس والروم في أمته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأنس بن مالك
rows.claim: After Mecca’s conquest, the Prophet promised his community Persian and Roman dominion; hypocrites and Jews mocked the prospect, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: لما فتح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مكة ووعد أمته ملك فارس والروم

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: In a trench report transmitted through ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, the Prophet’s blows on a rock flashed images of the palaces of Hira, Khosrow, Busra, and Sanaʿa; Gabriel promised the community would prevail over them, and the besieged believers recognized the promise (33:22).
rows.anchor: أضاءت لي منها قصور الحيرة ومدائن كسرى كأنها أنياب الكلاب

rows.speaker: المنافقون
rows.claim: Hypocrites mocked the promise that Muslims would see and conquer Khosrow’s cities while they were too frightened to emerge from the trench; the revelation of this verse answered their derision.
rows.anchor: فأنزل القرآن: وإذ يقول المنافقون والذين في قلوبهم مرض ما وعدنا الله ورسوله إلا غرورا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some grammarians say the mīm in Allāhumma replaces the deleted vocative yāʾ in yā Allāh; since two letters were removed, two replacement mīms assimilated, accounting for the doubled mīm and accusative form.
rows.anchor: إنما أدخل الميم في آخره بدلا من حرف النداء المحذوف من أوله لأن أصله (يا الله)

rows.speaker: الآخرون
rows.claim: Other grammarians reject that account because Arabic uses mīm even with vocative yāʾ, citing al-Farrāʾ’s verse. They derive Allāhumma from Allāh plus umm, with the vocative omitted and the hamza later dropped; lāhum is another shortened form.
rows.anchor: سمعنا العرب يدخل الميم فيه مع ياء النداء وأنشد الفراء:

rows.speaker: الآخرون
rows.claim: This alternative derives the prayer from Allāh plus umm, originally an appeal to direct or bring goodness; usage blended the word, dropped its hamza, and also produced lāhum and sometimes a shortened mīm.
rows.anchor: أصله الله في الدعاء. بمعنى (يا الله) ضم إليها أم وحذف حرف النداء.

rows.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
rows.claim: Abū Rajāʾ says the mīm in Allāhumma gathers seventy divine names; a divine saying calls God owner of kings and their hearts, says obedience brings merciful rulers and disobedience brings punishment, and urges repentance rather than cursing rulers.
rows.anchor: هذه الميم في قوله: (اللهم) : تجمع سبعين اسما من أسمائه عز وجل مالك الملك

rows.speaker: مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr interpret the kingdom bestowed and removed as the kingdom of prophethood.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير: يعني ملك النبوة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies Muhammad and his Companions as those granted rule, and Abū Jahl and Quraysh’s leading men as those stripped of it.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: تؤتي الملك من تشاء: محمد وأصحابه، وتنزع الملك ممن تشاء: أبي جهل وصناديد قريش.

rows.speaker: معتصم
rows.claim: Muʿtaṣim says the Arabs receive rule while the Romans, Persians, and other peoples lose it.
rows.anchor: قال معتصم: تؤتي الملك من تشاء: العرب. وتنزع الملك ممن تشاء: الروم والعجم وسائر الأمم.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says God granted rule to the prophets and ordered people to obey them, then removed it from tyrants and ordered people to oppose them.
rows.anchor: السدي: تؤتي الملك من تشاء: آتى الله الأنبياء وأمر العباد بطاعتهم.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation says Adam and his descendants receive the kingdom, while Iblīs and his host lose it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تؤتي الملك من تشاء: آدم وولده، وتنزع الملك ممن تشاء إبليس وجنده.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says David receives rule and Goliath loses it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تؤتي الملك من تشاء: داود. وتنزع الملك ممن تشاء: جالوت.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading says the jinn Sakhr receives rule while Solomon is deprived of it; Solomon’s lowly food and dress and his seeking the company of a poor person illustrate humility before God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تؤتي الملك من تشاء: صخرا. وتنزع الملك ممن تشاء: سليمان (عليه السلام)

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The same account depicts Solomon feeding the serving women bread, eating barley bread, wearing a patched garment, avoiding looking at the sky for forty years from fear of God, and sitting beside a poor person while calling himself poor.
rows.anchor: وكان يلبس المرقعة ولم ينظر أربعين سنة إلى السماء تخشيا لله.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further interpretation makes kingship mastery of the self: when desire overcomes a person, he takes desire as a god (45:23).
rows.anchor: ملك النفس حتى يغلبه هواه ويتخذه إلها. كما قال الله عز وجل أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه .

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poem supports the self-mastery interpretation by calling control of oneself a kingship unmatched among people, which makes its possessor free.
rows.anchor: ملكت نفسي فذاك ملك … ما مثله للأنام ملك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is the kingdom of well-being, linked to the verse saying God made people kings (5:20).
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو ملك العافية. قال الله تعالى: وجعلكم ملوكا

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet says that whoever wakes secure at home, healthy, and with a day’s food has been given the whole world.
rows.anchor: من أصبح منكم آمنا في سربه. معافى في بدنه، وعنده قوت يومه فكأنما حيزت له الدنيا بحذافيرها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is contentment; the Prophet calls the day-to-day contented the community’s kings and criticizes rejecting that provision without thankful patience.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو القناعة. قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ملوك أمتي القانع يوما بيوم

rows.speaker: ابن المبارك
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mubārak recounts visiting the ill, distressed Sufyan al-Thawrī, using an onion to make him sneeze and feel better; Sufyan praised him as a jurist and doctor, and Ibn al-Mubārak said he spoke from experience.
rows.anchor: فوجدته مريضا شارب دواء، وبه غم شديد فسلمت عليه، وقلت: ما لك يا عبد الله؟

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: In Ibn al-Mubārak’s reported dialogue, Sufyan says the true people are jurists, kings are ascetics, nobles are God-fearing, the rabble are hadith writers who exploit people for money, and the lowly are oppressors.
rows.anchor: فقلت: أخبرني ما الناس؟ قال: الفقهاء. قلت: فما الملوك؟ قال: الزهاد

rows.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Yaḥyā interprets the granted kingdom as rule over the lowly self and mastery of Satan, who moves through human beings like blood.
rows.anchor: تؤتي الملك من تشاء: يعني الملك على المهين وقهر الشيطان.

rows.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the kingdom mastery of spiritual knowledge, given to the sorcerers, and removed from Iblīs and Balʿam.
rows.anchor: يعني ملك المعرفة، كما آتى السحرة: وتنزع الملك ممن تشاء، كما نزع من إبليس وبلعام.

rows.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
rows.claim: Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl interprets the kingdom as Paradise, granted to believers and removed from disbelievers and the people of Hell; he cites the ‘great kingdom’ (76:20).
rows.anchor: تؤتي الملك من تشاء: يعني ملك الجنة كما آتى المؤمنين قال الله تعالى: وملكا كبيرا

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان
rows.claim: Abū ʿUthmān interprets kingdom as being granted guidance to faith and obedience.
rows.anchor: أبو عثمان: أراد (بالملك) : توفيق للإيمان والطاعة.

rows.speaker: بعض زهاد اليمن
rows.claim: An unnamed Yemeni ascetic interprets the kingdom as standing in prayer at night.
rows.anchor: إنه سمع بعض زهاد اليمن يقول: هو قيام الليل.

rows.speaker: الشبلي
rows.claim: Al-Shiblī interprets the kingdom as independence from both created worlds through dependence on the Creator.
rows.anchor: الشبلي: الاستغناء بالمكون عن الكونين.

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī says God reminds boastful kings that their rule is fleeting through the promise that He grants and removes it.
rows.anchor: افتخر الملوك بالملك. فأخبرهم الله تعالى أن الملك [زائل] عندهم لقوله تعالى: تؤتي الملك من تشاء

rows.speaker: الحكماء
rows.claim: The sages say the verse declares God’s complete power: one capable of perfection can do a thing and its opposite, granting or taking away rule.
rows.anchor: هذا إخبار عن كمال القدرة. وأن القادر على الكمال هو القادر على الشيء وضده

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ interprets honor as given to the Emigrants and Helpers and humiliation as inflicted on Persia and Rome.
rows.anchor: قال عطا: تعز من تشاء: المهاجرين والأنصار، وتذل من تشاء: فارس والروم.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says Muhammad and his companions were honored when they entered Mecca with ten thousand, while Abū Jahl’s associates were humiliated when their heads were cut off and cast into the well.
rows.anchor: تعز من تشاء: محمدا وأصحابه حين دخلوا مكة وعشرة آلاف ظاهرين عليها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation locates honor in faith and spiritual knowledge and humiliation in abandonment and deprivation.
rows.anchor: تعز من تشاء: بالإيمان والمعرفة. وتذل من تشاء: بالخذلان والحرمان.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation says God honors by granting property and authority and humiliates by removing rule and empowering an enemy over the person.
rows.anchor: تعز من تشاء: بالتمليك والتسليط. وتذل من تشاء: بسلب الملك وتسليط عدوه عليه.

rows.speaker: الوراق
rows.claim: Al-Warrāq says honor comes from mastering the self and resisting desire, while humiliation comes from following desire.
rows.anchor: الوراق: تعز من تشاء: بقهر النفس ومخالفة الهوى. وتذل من تشاء: باتباع الهوى.

rows.speaker: الكياني
rows.claim: Al-Kiyānī says honor is mastery over Satan, while humiliation is Satan gaining mastery over people.
rows.anchor: الكياني: تعز من تشاء: بقهره الشيطان. وتذل من تشاء: بقهر الشيطان لنا.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation links honor with contentment and acceptance and humiliation with disgrace and greed.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تعز من تشاء: بالقناعة والرضا. وتذل من تشاء: بالخزي والطمع.

rows.speaker: بنان الحمال
rows.claim: Banan al-Ḥammāl’s aphorism says greed makes a free person enslaved, whereas contentment makes a slave free.
rows.anchor: الحر عبد ما طمع. والعبد حر ما قنع.

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb pictures wealth and honor wandering until they meet contentment and settle there.
rows.anchor: خرج الغنى والعز يجولان فلقيا القناعة فاستقرا

rows.speaker: عيسى عليه السلام
rows.claim: Jesus tells his disciples they are richer than kings because they own nothing and desire nothing, while kings possess things that never suffice them.
rows.anchor: أنتم ليس عندكم شيء ولا تريدونها، وعندهم أشياء ولا تكفيهم.

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī’s poem says contentment with basic provision preserves dignity and frees a person from ambitions that may bring death.
rows.anchor: ألا يا نفس أن ترضي بقوت … فأنت عزيزة أبدا غنية

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: Another poet calls contentment a source of all dignity and advises making it one’s capital, joined with piety as one’s trade.
rows.anchor: أفادتني القناعة كل عز … وهل عز أعز من القناعة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says God honors through sincerity and humiliates through ostentation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تعز من تشاء: بالإخلاص، وتذل من تشاء: بالرياء.

rows.speaker: الحسن بن الفضل
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Faḍl links one outcome with Paradise and vision and the other with Fire and veiling; the transmitted text repeats ‘humiliate’ in both clauses.
rows.anchor: وتذل من تشاء: بالجنة والرؤيا. وتذل من تشاء: بالنار والحجاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘In Your hand is good’ also means good and evil; mentioning good alone suffices because it is better and more prevalent, as ‘garments protect you from heat’ also means cold (16:81).
rows.anchor: بيدك الخير: يعني الخير والشر، فأكتفي بذكر الخير فإنه الأفضل والأغلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes part of one night or day enter the other until the day is fifteen hours and the night nine, then reverses them; whatever is subtracted from one is added to the other, as in the image of night and day being rolled over each other (35:13).
rows.anchor: أي تدخل ما نقص من أحدهما في الآخر] حتى يكون النهار خمس عشرة ساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Quṭāmī’s use of iḥtifāran rather than ḥafran witnesses a verbal-noun form also used in the Qur’anic plant and devotion expressions (71:17; 73:8).
rows.anchor: ولم يقل حفرا قال الله تعالى: والله أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا . وقال: وتبتل إليه تبتيلا .

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators prohibit friendliness, alliance, flattery, and transactions with unbelievers except under their dominance or genuine fear among them: a believer may speak accommodatingly while inwardly faithful, to protect life, lawful property, and Muslim vulnerabilities, as ʿAmmār did.
rows.anchor: نهى الله عز وجل المؤمنين عن ملاطفة الكافرين وموالاتهم ومداهنتهم ومبايعتهم

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A man who had been tortured by Quraysh said his heart remained secure in faith; the Prophet told him to answer them the same way if the torture recurred, repeating this advice three times.
rows.anchor: قال: كيف كان قلبك؟ قال: مطمئن، قال: فإن عادوا لك فعد لهم مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd advises mixing with people, giving and greeting them as they like, while keeping one’s religion free of doubt or compromise.
rows.anchor: خالطوا الناس ونائلوهم وصافحوهم بما يشتهون، ودينكم لا يكون به ريبة.

rows.speaker: صعصعة بن صوحان
rows.claim: Ṣaʿṣaʿa counsels Usāma to show sincere allegiance to believers and good manners to unbelievers: good conduct satisfies the latter, but sincerity is owed to believers.
rows.anchor: خالص المؤمن وخالق الكافر فإن الكافر يرضى منك بالخلق الحسن

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد الصادق
rows.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq says dissimulation is obligatory and recounts hiding behind a mosque column when a man cursed him there so the man would not see him.
rows.anchor: التقية واجبة، وإني لأسمع الرجل في المسجد يشتمني فأستر بالسارية منه

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد الصادق
rows.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq says ostentation among believers is associating partners with God, while doing it in a hypocrite’s house is worship.
rows.anchor: الرياء مع المؤمن شرك ومع المنافق في داره عبادة.

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل عن مجاهد
rows.claim: Muʿādh, reporting from Mujāhid, says dissimulation was allowed at Islam’s beginning before the faith was established and Muslims were strong; now that God has strengthened Islam, Muslims should not fear their enemy.
rows.anchor: كانت التقية في جدة الإسلام قبل استحكام الدين وقوة المسلمين

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr rejects dissimulation in Islam, limiting it to wartime enemies, when asked during al-Ḥajjāj’s period about al-Ḥasan’s view that it is verbal while the heart remains faithful.
rows.anchor: ليس في الإسلام تقية إنما التقية في أهل الحرب.

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن المبارك
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mubārak’s poem condemns professing love for God while disobeying Him and argues that genuine love entails obedience to the beloved.
rows.anchor: لو كان حبك صادقا لأطعته … إن المحب لمن يحب مطيع

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A report from ʿĀʾisha says associating partners can be subtler than an ant on a smooth rock in a dark night; even loving injustice or hating justice is a lesser form of shirk, and religion is love and hatred for God, as the love-and-following verse says (3:31).
rows.anchor: الشرك أخف من دبيب النمل على الصفا في الليلة الظلماء، وأدناه أن تحب على شيء من الجور

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي
rows.claim: When the obedience verse was revealed, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubay objected that Muhammad equated obedience to himself with obedience to God and demanded to be loved as Christians love Jesus; the verse commanding obedience to God and the Messenger followed.
rows.anchor: فلما نزلت هذه الآية قال عبد الله بن أبي [لأصحابه: إن محمدا يجعل طاعته كطاعة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘If they turn away’ means turning away from obedience to God and the Messenger; God’s not loving the disbelievers means He does not approve their deeds, they have no share, and He will not forgive them.
rows.anchor: فإن تولوا: أعرضوا عن طاعتهما. فإن الله لا يحب الكافرين: لا يرضى فعلهم

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that obeying him is obeying God and obeying the ruler is obeying the Prophet; disobeying either is disobeying the one above him.
rows.anchor: من أطاعني فقد أطاع الله ومن أطاع الإمام فقد أطاعني

rows.speaker: كعب والحسن والكلبي ومطر الوراق ومحمد بن جعفر بن الزبير وابن جريج وابن زيد
rows.claim: These authorities interpret Jesus’s ‘taking’ as God’s seizing him and raising him from worldly life without death; they argue his people became Christians only after his raising, not after his death.
rows.anchor: فقال كعب والحسن والكلبي ومطر الوراق ومحمد بن جعفر بن الزبير وابن جريج وابن زيد: معناه: إني قابضك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of this view takes ‘I will raise you to Me’ to mean that God raises Jesus intact and beyond their reach, as when something is taken in full; it is supported by Jesus’s statement ‘when You took me’ (5:117).
rows.anchor: إني رافعك إلي وافيا لن ينالوا منك. من قولهم: توفيت كذا واستوفيته أي أخذته تاما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second lexical explanation takes tawaffaytuka as ‘I handed you over,’ from the idiom ‘I delivered such-and-such from him.’
rows.anchor: إني مسلمك، من قولهم: توفيت منه كذا أي سلمته.

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas interprets Jesus’s taking as sleep: God put him to sleep and raised him away from his people, comparing sleep to death and citing God’s taking people at night and taking souls in sleep and death (6:60; 39:42).
rows.anchor: معناه أني منيمك ورافعك إلي من قومك، يدل عليه قوله: وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains ‘let us implore’ as supplicating humbly.
rows.anchor: ثم نبتهل: نتضرع في الدعاء. قاله ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil explains ‘let us implore’ as making the prayer sincere.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: نخلص في الدعاء.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī explains the word as striving and exerting oneself in prayer.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: نجهد ونبالغ في الدعاء.

rows.speaker: الكسائي وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and Abū ʿUbayda explain the word as invoking a curse on the liar and cite the expression ‘God’s curse upon him.’
rows.anchor: الكسائي وأبو عبيدة: نلتعن بقول: لعن الله الكاذب منا

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labīd is cited for a usage of the imploring word in a line about the arrival of leaders and Time looking toward them with favor.
rows.anchor: قال لبيد: في قدوم سادة من قولهم نظر الدهر إليهم فابتهل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause ‘then let us make’ is grammatically coordinated with ‘let us implore.’
rows.anchor: فنجعل: عطف على قوله: نبتهل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘God’s curse’ is a verbal noun, and ‘the liars’ means those of either side who lie about Jesus.
rows.anchor: لعنت الله: مصدر. على الكاذبين: منا ومنكم في أمر عيسى

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Najran delegation postponed the challenge to consult; their leader al-ʿĀqib warned that Muhammad was a prophet and that no people who challenged a prophet survived, urging them to preserve their religion by making peace.
rows.anchor: والله ما لاعن قوم نبيا قط فعاش كبيرهم ولا نبت صغيرهم

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: At the appointed meeting the Prophet came with al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn, Fāṭima, and ʿAlī, telling them to say amen when he prayed; Najran’s bishop recognized faces whose prayer could move a mountain and advised against the challenge, so they declined.
rows.anchor: يا أبا القاسم قد رأينا أن لا نلاعنك، وأن نتركك على دينك ونثبت على ديننا.

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: After the delegation refused both the challenge and conversion, the Prophet offered Muslim rights and duties, then threatened war; they said they could not fight the Arabs and agreed to pay two thousand garments annually, half in Ṣafar and half in Rajab.
rows.anchor: نصالحك على أن لا تغزونا ولا تخيفنا ولا تردنا عن ديننا على أن نؤدي إليك كل عام ألفي سكة

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet says punishment had descended on Najran: had the parties invoked curses, they would have become apes and pigs, the valley would have burned, and all Najran and its Christians would have perished within a year.
rows.anchor: إن العذاب قد نزل في أهل نجران ولو تلاعنوا لمسخوا قردة وخنازير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘If they turn away’ means they turn away from faith.
rows.anchor: إن هذا لهو القصص الحق إلى فإن تولوا: أعرضوا عن الإيمان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The corruptors are those who worship someone other than God and call people to worship another.
rows.anchor: فإن الله عليم بالمفسدين: الذين يعبدون غير الله ويدعون الناس إلى عبادة غيره.

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The occasion is a dispute between Najran’s Christians and Jews over whether Abraham was Christian or Jewish; the Prophet rejects both claims, says Abraham was a ḥanīf and that he follows his religion, and calls them to Islam.
rows.anchor: وقالت اليهود: بل كان يهوديا وأنهم على دينه وأولى الناس به. فقال لهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: كلا الفريقين بريء من إبراهيم

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The two groups answer that Muhammad wants them to treat him as a lord, like Christians treat Jesus or Jews treat Ezra, and the verse inviting them to an equal word is revealed.
rows.anchor: فقالت اليهود: يا محمد ما تريد إلا أن نتخذك ربا كما اتخذت النصارى عيسى ربا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawaʾ means justice or equality; Ibn Masʿūd used it for the middle, and the middle is called fair because the fairest and best matters lie in the center, as in ‘the middle of Hell’ (37:55).
rows.anchor: عدل بيننا وبينكم وكذلك كان يقولها ابن مسعود قال: دعا فلان إلى السواء أي إلى النصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawaʾ is a verbal noun used as an adjective for ‘word’; a fatḥa lengthens its vowel, while kasra or ḍamma shortens it, and the Qur’anic ‘an even place’ illustrates the latter form (20:58).
rows.anchor: وسواء نعت للكلمة إلا أنه مصدر والمصادر لا تثنى ولا تجمع ولا تؤنث.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes the clause beginning an lā naʿbuda as nominative, with an implied ‘it is,’ meaning that we worship none but God.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: محله رفع [بمعنى أنه لا نعبد]

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another grammatical analysis makes the clause accusative by removing a preposition, with the sense ‘that we worship none but God.’
rows.anchor: وقيل: محله نصب بنزع حرف الصفة معناه: بأن لا نعبد إلا الله.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third analysis makes the clause genitive as an apposition to ‘word,’ meaning ‘come to not worship anyone but God.’
rows.anchor: وقيل: محله خفض بدلا من الكلمة أي تعالوا أن لا نعبد إلا الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not taking one another as lords means rejecting the Jews’ and Christians’ practice of making their scholars and monks lords besides God (9:31).
rows.anchor: ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا أربابا من دون الله: كما فعلت اليهود والنصارى.

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima interprets taking one another as lords as their bowing or prostrating to each other.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة: هو سجود بعضهم لبعض.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the command forbids obeying anyone in acts of disobedience; a report likens obeying a creature against God to prostrating to someone else.
rows.anchor: لا تطع في المعاصي أحدا، وفي الخبر من أطاع مخلوقا في معصية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the People of the Book turn away, the Muslims are to tell them to witness that they are sincere in affirming God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: أنتم لهم اشهدوا بأنا مسلمون: مخلصون بالتوحيد

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet’s letter to Heraclius and Rome’s rulers quotes this verse after inviting them to Islam, promising a doubled reward if they accept, and warning that refusal leaves them with the burden of their subjects’ sins.
rows.anchor: فإني أدعوك إلى الإسلام أسلم تسلم. أسلم يؤتك الله أجرك مرتين.
